title: The APT Foundation Sponsors Leopard Sharks
author: Ian
body:
In support of Conservation International’s Leopard Shark Population Recovery Program, the APT Foundation has sponsored 2 sharks and donated $2,000 to the project.

As part of the sponsorship, the APT Foundation held an internal competition to name the Shark duo, asking APT Travel Group staff to submit their suggestions.” The always funny “SharkyMcSharkFace” was floated around, though sense prevailed and the group decided on “Leonie” and “Leonard.”

These sharks were recently tagged off the coast of Stradbroke Island in Queensland, where a team of 6 researchers caught and released these sharks from the shallow waters. The research team included Christine Dudgeon from University of Queensland who is a world-renowned expert in leopard sharks and has been studying this population for 18 years.

The tagging will allow researchers to gather data from the sharks for up to 10 years. The knowledge gained will help improve Conservation Internationals shark repopulation program, resulting in successfully hatching and raising more aquaria-sources pups into Raja Ampat. This is a world first attempt to boost a wild population in such a way.
